title: Nonlinear Reshaping of Gaussian Water Wave Packets
authors: Zibo Zheng, Takuji Waseda, C. Martijn de Sterke, Andrea Blanco-Redondo, Amin Chabchoub
abstract: The propagation of narrowband wave packets is a classical problem with broad relevance across nonlinear wave physics. Within the framework of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation, solitons are known to propagate without changing shape, whereas Gaussian envelopes may undergo substantial reshaping depending on the balance between dispersion and nonlinearity. Here, we combine laboratory experiments with numerical simulations to systematically investigate the evolution of hydrodynamic Gaussian wave packets over a wide range of amplitudes and spectral bandwidths. We show that when the envelope amplitude and width match those of the stationary NLSE soliton solution, the wave packet propagates steadily in the wave flume. More generally, by varying the amplitude of the Gaussian envelope, the wave packet may undergo either dispersive broadening or nonlinear focusing, resembling the dynamics of Satsuma-Yajima breathers. These findings may facilitate the controlled generation and manipulation of localized wave packets in a variety of nonlinear dispersive systems, including optics, plasmas, and Bose-Einstein condensates.
summary: This work systematically studies how Gaussian wave packets reshape when propagating in deep water, governed by nonlinear dispersive effects. By comparing lab experiments with numerical solutions of the NLSE and MNLSE, the authors map out regimes ranging from dispersive broadening to strong nonlinear focusing. The findings provide crucial guidance for controlling localized wave energy in various nonlinear physical systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the nonlinear reshaping and evolution of Gaussian wave packets propagating in deep water.
main_result: The wave packet evolution depends critically on the balance between dispersion and nonlinearity, showing steady propagation when parameters match the NLSE soliton, but requiring higher-order corrections (MNLSE) in strongly focusing regimes.
method: The study combines laboratory experiments measuring wave profiles with numerical simulations solving the Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation (NLSE) and its modified version (MNLSE).
model_or_system: The physical system is deep-water surface waves, modeled by the wave envelope $A(x, t)$ governed by the NLSE or MNLSE, derived from the Euler equations.
key_observables: Wave packet evolution (broadening, focusing, steady propagation), envelope amplitude, and width.
important_parameters: The dimensionless amplitude factor $N$ (varied from 0.36 to 1.8) and the ratio of characteristic lengths $L_D/L_{NL}$.
main_assumptions: The NLSE is an approximation valid for small steepness; the MNLSE is used when higher-order effects become significant during strong focusing.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spatial evolution of Gaussian envelopes across different regimes (dispersion-dominated, quasi-stationary, focusing), comparing experimental data with NLSE and MNLSE predictions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem, derives the governing equations (NLSE/MNLSE), details the methodology (experimental setup and numerical solvers), presents results across varying nonlinearity regimes, and concludes with acknowledgements.
why_interesting: While focused on classical water waves, the underlying mathematical framework—the nonlinear Schrödinger equation and its higher-order corrections—is central to nonlinear wave physics relevant to quantum optics and nonlinear wave propagation in various media.
